lead: Black as the sea at night. Cuttlefish ink dyes every grain of rice and concentrates the flavour of the Mediterranean in a dish that surprises as much by its look as by its intensity. With alioli, always.

Black rice is the most dramatic rice in Valencia. Not the most complicated — the technique is exactly the same as for seafood paella — but the most surprising for the diner seeing it for the first time. A completely black rice on the plate, steaming, with the concentrated aroma of the sea, and on top a spoonful of creamy white alioli. The visual contrast is relentless.

What separates a mediocre black rice from an exceptional one comes down to two things: the homemade fumet — made with prawn heads and shells, fish bones and morralla — and the patience of the sofrito. If the broth is poor, black rice is just rice dyed black. If the fumet is rich, black rice is a complete marine experience.

items.title: Arròs Negre · The Rice of the Dark Sea
items.subtitle: Squid or cuttlefish ink · Intense black colour · Deep marine flavour
items.body: Black rice — arròs negre in Valencian — is one of the most spectacular and surprising rices in Mediterranean cooking. Its intense black colour does not come from any exotic ingredient, but from the natural ink of the squid or cuttlefish: a liquid that cephalopods use to escape their predators and that, in the kitchen, gives the rice a unique colour and a concentrated, briny, deep marine flavour. It is a dry rice in the paella style, cooked in the same vessel and with the same technique, but with a completely different visual and gustatory identity. Born in the Mediterranean, its paternity is disputed by the fishermen of Valencia, Castellón, Alicante, Tarragona and the Costa Brava — which says a lot about how deeply rooted it is along the whole Levante coast.
facts: Dry rice, paella style · Cooked in a flat paella pan · Always served with alioli · Cuttlefish as the star ingredient

items.title: The Ink · The Ingredient That Changes Everything
items.subtitle: Cuttlefish or squid ink · Concentrated marine flavour · Unique colour and aroma
items.body: The ink is the soul of black rice. It is known that as far back as the 17th century squid ink was used to give flavour and colour to the dishes of Mediterranean fishermen. In black rice, the ink is added diluted in the hot fumet before it goes into the sofrito, dyeing every grain of rice black and contributing a unique marine flavour. Cuttlefish is the preferred cephalopod for this dish — tastier than squid — and you can use either the natural ink of fresh cuttlefish or the little sachets of ink sold in the frozen section of the supermarket. The ink of fresh cuttlefish is extracted carefully from the sac, mixed with a little stock and added. The result: a rice completely black on the outside but with the grain perfectly cooked and full of marine flavour inside.
facts: Natural ink from fresh cuttlefish or frozen sachets (4–5 g/sachet) · Always dilute in the fumet before adding

items.title: The Sofrito and the Fumet · The Two Bases of the Dish
items.subtitle: Sofrito of onion, garlic and tomato · Fumet of morralla or prawn heads · The difference shows
items.body: As with all the great Valencian rices, the secret of black rice lies in the sofrito and the fumet. The sofrito is prepared by gently sweating very finely chopped onion — with patience, until it is translucent and sweet —, adding garlic, sweet paprika and grated tomato. The cuttlefish is first seared over high heat, removed and added to the sofrito. The fumet must be concentrated and tasty: it is made with prawn heads, white fish bones or morralla (small rockfish), and it provides the marine depth that black rice needs. Once the sofrito is ready, the rice is added, briefly sautéed, and the hot fumet with the diluted ink goes in. The cooking time is the same as paella: 10 minutes over high heat and 8–10 over medium-low heat.
facts: Fumet: always hot before adding · Proportion: 2–2.5 parts fumet to 1 of rice · High heat at the start

items.title: The Alioli · The Essential Accompaniment
items.subtitle: Garlic and oil emulsion · The black and white contrast · The final touch
items.body: Black rice is always served with alioli. The visual contrast — the completely black rice with a spoonful of creamy white alioli on top — is one of the most beautiful moments in Valencian cooking. But it is the contrast of flavour that makes black rice with alioli an extraordinary dish: the marine intensity of the black rice, the bitter, powerful touch of the garlic, the softness of the oil. Authentic Valencian alioli — garlic, oil and salt, emulsified by hand in the mortar — is the ideal. The version with egg or milk is easier and also works. In the Comunitat Valenciana, alioli also accompanies arroz a banda, fideuà and other seafaring preparations. The Iberians of the region were already eating it before the arrival of the Romans.
facts: Authentic alioli: garlic + oil + salt · Emulsified in a mortar · The version with egg is easier but different

items.title: Variations · From Classic to Contemporary
items.subtitle: With lobster · With baby squid · In an earthenware dish in the oven · Black fideuà
items.body: The base recipe — cuttlefish, prawns, ink and fumet — is the most widespread and authentic, but black rice allows notable variations. The version with lobster is the most festive and generous, common in leading restaurants. The one made with small fresh baby squid gives a more delicate texture. In some restaurants it is briefly gratinéed in the oven to create a crust on the surface. Black fideuà — with noodles instead of rice and squid ink — is the variation first popularised by the restaurant Puerta del Mar in Valencia, going viral on social media. In Castellón there is also a variation with black rice in an earthenware dish in the style of baked rice, which combines the technique and flavours of both traditions.
facts: Most festive variation: with lobster · Viral variation: black fideuà · With baby squid: more delicate · Baked: also exists

items.title: Cuttlefish, not squid
items.body: Cuttlefish is tastier and the ink more concentrated — the result is rounder

items.title: Fumet always hot
items.body: Cold broth breaks the rice’s cooking — keep it boiling before adding

items.title: Patient sofrito
items.body: The onion must be sweated very slowly until translucent and almost caramelised

items.title: Ink diluted in fumet
items.body: Never add the ink directly — dilute it in the hot fumet before adding

items.title: Don’t touch the rice
items.body: As in paella, once the rice is spread it is not stirred — the grain must stay loose

items.title: Rest 5 minutes
items.body: Turn off the heat and let it rest covered before serving with the alioli on the side

blocks.title: What you should know about black rice
items: Authentic black rice has cuttlefish, not chicken — it is a seafaring rice, nothing to do with Valencian paella
Alioli is a must — without it the dish is incomplete. The black/white contrast is part of the experience
The black colour comes from cuttlefish or squid ink — the rice itself is white, dyed during cooking by the fumet and the ink
No vegetables are added — no green pepper, no beans, no asparagus. It is a sea rice, pure and direct
Cuttlefish is better than squid for this dish — its ink is more concentrated and the flesh more tender and tasty
It is a midday dish — like all Valencian rices. It is made fresh and eaten freshly made
